title: The Moonbridge Surcharge
story: Mr 6 reaches the Moonbridge carrying 240 gold crowns to buy medicine for a snowed-in village. Tolliver the Bridge Appraiser, a stooped heron-headed clerk with a stamp for a beak, announces a toll of 35% of everything a traveler carries. 'But,' he sniffs, 'honest travelers who state the exact amount left over may cross for free — and keep it all.'
question: If Tolliver's toll were 35% of Mr 6's 240 gold crowns, how many crowns would be left over after paying it?
solution: Find the toll: 35% of 240 = 0.35 x 240 = 84 crowns.
Subtract it from what he carries: 240 - 84 = 156 crowns.
praise: Finding 35% of 240 was exactly the right first move - the toll itself just needed subtracting from the 240 to get the leftover.
hint: First work out what 35% of 240 actually is, then ask: how much of the 240 would still be in the pouch?
victory: Tolliver stamps his own forehead in shock, squawks 'CORRECT!', and lifts the gate - Mr 6 strolls across with every single crown still jingling.
imagePrompt: A heron-headed toll clerk in a too-small coat gaping at a brave little numeral-six knight on a moonlit silver bridge over fog, cool blue light.
